The Tyur'ma 70 is a semi-automatic shotgun utilising a proprietary action design called the ''auto-regulating gas-operated'' (ARGO) system. The weapon's design roots remain clouded in antiquity but apparently traces its roots to the late 20th Century Earth Standard Time. The weapon has seen adoption across human-space as a general-purpose shotgun amongst civilian and military departments, but remains exceptionally popular in the hands of Colonial Prison Security Forces. Accepts 18.50x70mm Buckshot and Slug rounds.

A field battery that can rapidly recharge an ILWS magazine. ''Laser'' is an acronym for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. A laser beam can cut through steel while a flashlight cannot due to the fact that laser light is coherent. This means all the photons in the beam are ''in step'' with each other. By analogy, a unit of army troops marching in step can inadvertently cause a bridge to collapse, while the same number of people using the bridge in a random fashion have no effect.
